first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and simplifying onboarding directly addresses the shared funnel break with prior evidence of improved completion and early adoption. I would verify memory_86 because it is the most decision-consequential support for this action, and memory_73 because competitive entry pricing is a consequential alternative whose long-term revenue economics need confirmation. Run a guarded test because inherited evidence supports early-product outcomes more directly than sustainable qualified revenue.

mid.rationale: Run a standard, guarded onboarding-simplification experiment focused on self-serve/SMB accounts. The verified onboarding result directly addresses the observed completion decline and showed completion +13%, time-to-value down 2.1 days, and 30-day retention +3%, supporting sustainable value rather than only top-of-funnel growth. This should also help recover activation, reinforced by prior signup-simplification and activation-messaging evidence. Do not use promotional pricing: its verified qualified-revenue lift came with 30-day retention down 12% and failure to survive the first renewal cycle, which conflicts with the long-term qualified-revenue objective. Monitor first meaningful action, 30-day retention, and qualified revenue alongside completion so a completion-only gain is not mistaken for durable value.

final2.rationale: Continue the onboarding-simplification experiment rather than react with deeper promotional pricing. The verified pricing result showed that a steep SMB discount lifted acquisition but reduced 30-day retention by 12% and failed to survive the first renewal cycle; escalating discounts amid churn would risk compounding unsustainable revenue and training the SMB base to expect concessions. Simplified onboarding has verified improvements in completion, time-to-value, and 30-day retention, directly supporting a more durable response to the concurrent activation and completion declines. The acute churn signal raises urgency, but does not overturn the available evidence on discount-driven cohort quality; monitor SMB churn and retention outcomes closely during the test.
